newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market closed mostly down on Friday, with demand for money decreasing after three education funds made their debut on the Shanghai stock exchange today, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract plunged to 2.90 percent from 10 percent on Thursday.
Turnover fell to 4.43 million lots from 5.53 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"A fall in demands for money caused sharp drops in early-maturing contracts," said one local trader.
"The correction after a sharp rise on Thursday was mainly due to institutional selling and the fact there will be no new issues and listings of A shares early next week," he said.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up, encouraged by the strong performance of the most active seven-year bond, traders said. The bond that matures in Nov 2003 rose to 97.25 yuan from 96.49 yuan on Thursday.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 1.34 million lots from 2.80 million on Thursday.
"The first seven-year bond began to rally today after continued losses in the past days," one trader said.
"Many institutions which bought the seven-year bond at around 100 yuan were eager to support it," he added.
Traders expect the bond to go up next week.
